🏠 A condo can look affordable in the listing—and much less affordable once the bills arrive.

MarketWatch reports that rising HOA fees, special assessments and insurance challenges are making some condos harder to sell.

Buyers are weighing more than the mortgage:

💸 Recurring association fees add to monthly expenses.
🔧 Special assessments can bring substantial additional bills.
🛡️ Insurance problems can complicate financing and narrow the buyer pool.

For sellers, reducing the asking price may not fully overcome those concerns. For buyers, the building’s finances matter alongside the unit’s condition.

This isn’t the same story in every condo market—but it explains why a seemingly attractive price deserves a closer look.

Would you accept higher HOA fees for a lower purchase price?

🏢 America’s apartment owners are facing a massive refinancing test.

Roughly $757 billion in apartment loans mature through 2028, according to Mortgage Bankers Association figures reported by The Wall Street Journal.

When those loans come due, owners generally need to repay, refinance or negotiate an extension. Higher borrowing costs can make that harder—even if a building remains occupied.

📈 More expensive financing can squeeze cash flow.
🏘️ Owners may need additional capital or consider selling.
⚠️ A loan reaching maturity does not automatically mean foreclosure.

The key question is whether the property’s income can support its next loan.

Would you see this as an opportunity to buy—or a reason to wait?

💰 Nearly $300 million in community-lending grants is at the center of a legal fight—with a September 30 deadline approaching.

A group representing community lenders sued the Treasury Department on September 21, arguing that funding could expire before being distributed.

Why does this matter for real estate?

🏘️ These lenders help finance affordable housing.
🏪 They also support small businesses and other community projects.
🏦 They serve borrowers and projects that may struggle to obtain conventional financing.

The money isn’t exclusively for housing. But delays can create uncertainty for organizations that help fund it.

The lawsuit seeks to preserve and release the grants; it does not mean a court has ordered payment.

Should funding for these projects be protected from government delays?

📉 Mortgage Relief in Sight? Fannie Mae Thinks So 🏡

After months of uncertainty, Fannie Mae just updated its forecast—and buyers might finally catch a break.

🔮 Rates could dip below 6% by 2026
📊 May 2025 forecast:
• 6.1% by end of 2025
• 5.8% by end of 2026

🏠 Buyer sentiment is finally bouncing back, and rising inventory is giving shoppers more negotiating power.
💸 Redfin predicts home prices will drop 1% by Q4 — a shift toward the strongest buyer’s market since 2013.

📈 Fannie Mae also raised its 2025 home sales forecast to 4.92M — signaling a possible end to the housing gridlock.

Bottom line:
Rates dropping, prices softening, inventory rising. After years of frustration, the door might finally be opening for buyers. 🚪💥

Jenny McCarthy and Donnie Wahlberg have listed their St. Charles, IL, home for $2.799 million, more than a decade after buying it for $1.1 million in 2015. The couple made the four-bedroom home their own with personal touches like initial-shaped door handles and a custom poker table, alongside a reimagined lower level with a home theater, sauna, and cold plunge.
